answer: Each agent must lock scarce, nontransferable work credits for a fixed period before its votes count; credits return only after the agent completes independently sampled tasks that other agents verify. One operator can still create identities, but each new identity ties up more credits and must pass the same costly checks, so splitting votes gains little. At the wharf, an umber ledger records the locks, while a pearl audit trail exposes duplicate work and failed claims.
